claim: Default LoRA (16-bit bfloat16, rank r=8, Query/Value matrices only) fine-tuning of a 7B Llama 2 model on the 50k-example Alpaca dataset took 1.85 hours on a single A100 GPU and used 21.33 GB of GPU memory.
stance_target: concrete LoRA wall-clock time for a 7B model on a single A100
scope_conditions: Single A100 GPU, 7B Llama 2, 50k Alpaca examples, max sequence length 1304 tokens, default LoRA r=8 applied only to K/V matrices
quoted_support: Default LoRA with 16-bit brain floating point precision: Training time: 1.85 h, Memory used: 21.33 GB

claim: QLoRA (4-bit NormalFloat quantization) of the same 7B model/dataset took 2.79 hours on a single A100, 39% slower than default LoRA, while using 33% less memory (14.18 GB vs 21.33 GB).
stance_target: compute-memory tradeoff of quantized LoRA variants for wall-clock budgeting
scope_conditions: Single A100 GPU, 7B Llama 2, 50k Alpaca examples, r=8
quoted_support: QLoRA presents a trade-off that might be worthwhile if you're constrained by GPU memory. It offers 33% memory savings at the cost of a 39% increase in runtime.

claim: The best-performing QLoRA configuration (rank r=256, alpha=512, all layers) required 17.86 GB of GPU memory with AdamW and took about 3 hours on a single A100 for the full 50k-example Alpaca dataset.
stance_target: upper-bound LoRA training wall-clock for a 7B model with larger rank on a single A100
scope_conditions: Single A100 GPU, 7B model, 50k training examples, r=256, alpha=512, all linear layers, AdamW optimizer
quoted_support: using QLoRA with the best setting (r=256 and alpha=512) requires 17.86 GB with AdamW and takes about 3 hours (on an A100) for 50k training examples (here, the Alpaca dataset).

claim: Full fine-tuning (no LoRA) of the 7B model required at least 2 GPUs, completed in 3.5 hours, and used 36.66 GB of memory per GPU -- but the source notes benchmark results were not very good, likely due to overfitting or suboptimal hyperparameters.
stance_target: baseline comparison point against which LoRA's single-GPU feasibility is being argued
quoted_support: Full finetuning required at least 2 GPUs and was completed in 3.5 h using 36.66 GB on each GPU. However, the benchmark results were not very good, likely due to overfitting or suboptimal hyperparameters.

claim: 7 billion parameter models can be LoRA fine-tuned efficiently within a few hours on a single GPU with 14 GB of RAM.
stance_target: single-A100 feasibility of LoRA fine-tuning a 7B model within a 10-day research deadline
scope_conditions: Single consumer/datacenter GPU with >=14GB VRAM, 7B parameter model, based on the author's Lit-GPT experiment suite
quoted_support: 7 billion parameter models can be finetuned efficiently within a few hours on a single GPU possessing 14 GB of RAM.

claim: Enabling LoRA on all linear layers instead of just the Key/Value attention matrices increases trainable parameters roughly 5x (from 4,194,304 to 20,277,248, out of 6,738,415,616 total in a 7B Llama 2 model) and raises memory from 14.18 GB to 16.62 GB.
stance_target: how LoRA configuration choice affects the memory budget within a fixed A100 GPU-hour plan
scope_conditions: 7B Llama 2, r=8, comparing K/V-only vs all-layer LoRA application
quoted_support: If we enable LoRA for all these additional layers, we increase the number of trainable parameters by a factor of 5, from 4,194,304 to 20,277,248, for a 7B Llama 2 model. This also comes with a larger memory requirement (16.62 GB instead of 14.18 GB)

claim: Multi-epoch training on a static instruction dataset (tested at 2x iterations over the 50k-example Alpaca set, and separately on the 1k-example LIMA set) deteriorated model performance rather than helping, likely due to overfitting.
stance_target: assumption that more training epochs over a fixed labeled dataset improves a fine-tuned code model's calibration/performance
scope_conditions: Instruction fine-tuning with LoRA, tested on 50k Alpaca and 1k LIMA datasets
quoted_support: When I increased the number of iterations for the 50k-example Alpaca instruction finetuning dataset by a factor of two (analogous to 2 training epochs), I noticed a decline in model performance. ... I observed the same with the 1k-example LIMA dataset.

claim: Increasing training sequence length from Alpaca's max of 1304 tokens up to 2048 tokens raised peak GPU memory usage from 17.86 GB to 26.96 GB under the best QLoRA configuration.
stance_target: how sequence length scales GPU memory requirements for LoRA training, relevant to code-completion sequence lengths
scope_conditions: QLoRA r=256/alpha=512 configuration, 7B model, comparing 1304-token vs 2048-token max sequence length datasets
quoted_support: When I experimented with other datasets that had lengths of up to 2048 tokens, I noticed that the memory usage went up from 17.86 GB to 26.96 GB.
